lead: This unit shows how a loaded beam bends: how to find slope and deflection at any point, and how to use energy ideas when integration is slow. After it you can set up the elastic curve, choose a deflection method, and solve a propped cantilever or fixed beam by compatibility.
about: The unit starts with the elastic curve and the relation EI y″ = M, then builds four ways to turn it into numbers: double integration (5.2), Macaulay's brackets (5.3), moment-area (5.4), and the conjugate beam (5.5). Superposition (5.6) lets you add standard cases instead of integrating again. Strain energy and Maxwell's theorem (5.7) give a second route to deflection. The last chapter (5.8) uses these tools with compatibility to analyse propped cantilevers, fixed beams and continuous beams, including support settlement. Each method is a different calculator for the same slope and deflection; the mechanics does not change.

chapters.idea: A bent beam follows an elastic curve whose curvature at any section is the bending moment divided by EI.
chapters.depth: Define x along the beam, y the deflection, EI the flexural rigidity. State the small-deflection relation 1/R = M/EI and its Cartesian form EI d²y/dx² = M. Fix one sign convention: y upward, sagging M positive; say the sign flips if y is taken downward. Give boundary conditions for fixed, simple and free ends. Show the chain EI y″ = M, EI y‴ = V, EI y⁗ = −w for downward w. Mention 'governing differential equation' and 'equation of the elastic curve' as other names. Keep to setting up, not integrating.

figure.title: From load to deflection
figure.aria: A block diagram runs from load to shear to moment to curvature, then integrates curvature to slope and slope to deflection.

chapters.example: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. EI = 5000 kN·m². Taking y upward and sagging moment positive, write M(x) and find the curvature at midspan.
chapters.trap: Mixing sign conventions: a sagging moment with y downward needs EI y″ = −M. Write the convention at the top of every answer.
chapters.prereq: Unit 3 (SFD and BMD); Unit 4 (bending stress and EI).

chapters.idea: Integrate EI y″ = M twice and use two boundary conditions to get slope and deflection.
chapters.depth: Direct integration method. Cover a simply supported beam with UDL and with a central point load (two regions), a cantilever with end load and with UDL. Show the two constants C₁, C₂ and how support conditions fix them: y = 0 at simple supports, y = 0 and y′ = 0 at a fixed end. Mention 'double integration method' and 'direct integration method'. Keep expressions symbolic before substituting numbers.

figure.aria: A plot shows the downward deflection of a simply supported beam under a UDL, zero at both supports and 11.25 mm down at midspan.

chapters.example: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a UDL of 4 kN/m. EI = 6000 kN·m². Find the midspan deflection and the slope at a support by double integration.
chapters.trap: Applying boundary conditions before integrating, or using one M(x) across a point load where M changes formula.
chapters.leave: Discontinuous loads to 5.3; indeterminate beams to 5.8.

chapters.idea: Macaulay's method writes one moment expression for the whole beam using bracket terms that switch on after each load.
chapters.depth: Define <x−a>ⁿ: zero when x < a, (x−a)ⁿ when x ≥ a. Cover point loads, applied moments, UDL starting at a, and UDL that ends (add a negative bracket term). Integrate brackets as <x−a>^{n+1}/(n+1), with no new constant per bracket. Apply y = 0 at supports. Mention 'singularity function method' and 'Macaulay's brackets'. Use for determinate beams; point to 5.8 for indeterminate use.

figure.title: Macaulay solution path
figure.aria: A flow chart shows reactions feeding one Macaulay moment expression, which is integrated twice and fixed by boundary conditions.

chapters.example: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a point load of 10 kN at 2 m from the left end and a UDL of 4 kN/m over the whole span. EI = 6000 kN·m². Use Macaulay's method to find the deflection under the point load.
chapters.trap: Evaluating a bracket with a negative argument instead of treating it as zero.

chapters.idea: The area under the M/EI diagram gives change in slope, and its first moment about a point gives tangential deviation.
chapters.depth: State both moment-area theorems. Theorem 1: θ_B − θ_A = area of M/EI between A and B. Theorem 2: t_B/A = moment of that area about B; t_B/A is the vertical distance of B from the tangent drawn at A. Explain sign and that t is not deflection unless the tangent is known. Use cantilever end load and simply supported UDL; moment diagram by parts. Mention 'Mohr's theorems' and 'area-moment method'. Keep conjugate beam separate.

figure.aria: A plot shows a triangular M/EI diagram for a cantilever with an end load, largest at the fixed end and zero at the free end.

chapters.example: A cantilever of length 3 m carries a point load of 8 kN at its free end. EI = 4000 kN·m². Find the free-end deflection and slope by the moment-area method.
chapters.trap: Using t_B/A as the absolute deflection when the tangent at A is not horizontal.
chapters.leave: Conjugate beam and superposition to 5.5 and 5.6.

chapters.idea: A conjugate beam loaded with the M/EI diagram has shear equal to real slope and moment equal to real deflection.
chapters.depth: Only a few universities teach this. Give support transformation: real fixed → conjugate free, real free → conjugate fixed, real simple → conjugate simple, real internal hinge → conjugate internal hinge. Load the conjugate beam with M/EI (sign according to chosen convention). Then V* = θ and M* = y. Use for determinate beams: simply supported with central load, cantilever with end load. Mention 'fictitious beam method' and 'conjugate beam method'.

figure.aria: A tree lists how each real support is replaced by its conjugate support.

chapters.example: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a central point load of 12 kN. EI = 5000 kN·m². Use the conjugate beam method to find the midspan deflection.
chapters.trap: Keeping the real supports instead of transforming them.

chapters.idea: In a linear elastic beam, slopes and deflections from separate load cases add algebraically.
chapters.depth: Only a few universities teach this. Give a short table of standard results: cantilever end load PL³/3EI, cantilever UDL wL⁴/8EI, simply supported central load PL³/48EI, simply supported UDL 5wL⁴/384EI. Cover splitting a combined load into standard cases, adding at the same point with signs, and using it for overhanging beams. Mention 'method of superposition' and 'superposition principle'. Do not use for nonlinear or large deflection.

figure.aria: A stack shows two standard deflection cases added to give the total midspan deflection.

chapters.example: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a UDL of 4 kN/m over the whole span and a central point load of 12 kN. EI = 6000 kN·m². Find the midspan deflection by superposition.
chapters.trap: Adding deflections at different points, or ignoring sign when loads act opposite.
chapters.leave: Nonlinear and large-deflection problems; indeterminate compatibility to 5.8.

chapters.idea: Strain energy in bending is U = ∫M²/(2EI)dx; its derivative with respect to a load gives the deflection under that load, and Maxwell's theorem links two reciprocal deflections.
chapters.depth: Derive U for pure bending and for a beam by integration. State Castigliano's theorem: ∂U/∂P = displacement in the direction of P. Use unit-load method briefly. State Maxwell's reciprocal theorem: deflection at A due to unit load at B equals deflection at B due to unit load at A; mention Betti's theorem. Apply to determinate beams. Mention 'energy method', 'Castigliano's theorem', 'unit load method', 'Betti-Maxwell theorem'. Leave leaf springs to Unit 6.

figure.title: Energy route to deflection
figure.aria: A block diagram shows load giving bending moment, then strain energy, whose partial derivative gives deflection.

chapters.example: A cantilever of length 2 m carries a point load of 6 kN at its free end. EI = 3000 kN·m². Use Castigliano's theorem to find the free-end deflection.
chapters.trap: Differentiating U before substituting M(P), or missing the factor 2 in U.
chapters.leave: Leaf springs and helical springs to Unit 6; failure theories to Unit 2.

chapters.idea: Extra supports make reactions redundant; compatibility of deflection at the redundant support supplies the missing equation.
chapters.depth: Define static indeterminacy for beams (number of extra reactions); leave 2D/3D frames to a structures course. Solve propped cantilever and fixed beam by choosing the prop or fixed-end moment as redundant and using a deflection result from 5.2–5.7. Give standard results: propped cantilever UDL prop reaction 3wL/8, fixed-end moment wL²/8; fixed beam central load end moment PL/8. Introduce Clapeyron's theorem of three moments for continuous beams, including different support settlement and end conditions. Mention 'theorem of three moments' and 'compatibility method'.

figure.aria: A tree groups indeterminate beams into propped cantilever, fixed beam and continuous beam.

chapters.example: A propped cantilever of span 4 m is fixed at A and simply supported at B. It carries a UDL of 6 kN/m over the whole span. EI = 5000 kN·m². Find the prop reaction at B and the fixed-end moment at A.
chapters.trap: Using the wrong redundant or dropping the settlement term in the three-moment equation.
chapters.leave: Frames and 3D indeterminacy to a structures course.

links: curvature equation becomes the integrated deflection
M/EI area comes from the same curvature relation
standard cases are added without re-integrating
Macaulay solves propped and fixed beams
compatibility uses energy or unit-load deflections
